column7: Faith is a bedrock concept in Christianity. Faith is such a commonly used word in Christianity that sometimes the meaning of the word is supplanted by subtle misconceptions and wrong understanding. But it’s not something you can hold in your hands-it’s something formed in your heart as you come to trust God. Persuasion is belief.
column8: Faith is a foundational concept in Christianity. Because the word faith is used so very frequently in Christianity, at times its meaning gets replaced by subtle misunderstandings or mistaken interpretations. Yet it is not something you can take in your hand - it is something that is formed in your heart as you come to trust God. Conviction is believing.

column6: The original emphasizes 'persuasion' as a key aspect of faith, while the back-translation shifts the focus to 'assurance', which alters the conceptual understanding of faith from an active belief to a more passive sense of certainty.
column7: So, what is faith? Persuasion! The Greek word ***pistis*** means persuasion, or the result of being persuaded. We are to have persuasion towards God. In English we might say faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, you hopefully have faith ‘**in’** your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you believe that they are being authentic and genuine. This trust should extend beyond what they’ve said, to extend to them in general.
column8: Then, what is faith? Assurance! The Greek ***pistis*** means assurance, or the result obtained by being persuaded. We are asked to have assurance toward God. In English, we might express faith (assurance) as ‘**in** God’. If you are married, hopefully you trust your spouse. That is, you believe your spouse ‘**in’**. You believe your spouse will do what they said, and that the person is faithful and genuine. This trust should extend beyond their words to the whole person.
